observations: The v0.10 lifecycle suite passed clean installation, repeat sync, v0.9 upgrade and rollback, conflict preservation, and uninstall restoration in isolated macOS homes under Python 3.9.6 and 3.14.5.

Native responses changed from PLAIN to TAGGED after one shared custom proof-label stance changed. Session and project overrides resolved through the same primitive authority after native hook trust was reviewed.

Manual mode and an autonomy denial prevented disposable writes, while an explicitly acknowledged bypass created its sentinel. Claude Code accepted the Auto selection but the tested Bedrock account could not execute native Auto because Sonnet 5 access was unavailable; the client reported the restriction and did not widen permissions.
Native PostToolUse execution delivered independent Review Card feedback for both files in one multi-file change while retaining a separate user hook.
Isolated gatherer and planner workers completed under native read restrictions; forced writes remained denied and planner publication stayed parent-mediated.
The stop gate reused an unchanged green result, reran for staged, untracked, and edited-untracked changes, and blocked a failing gate through its retry budget.
The full four-layer BMad review completed under Sonnet 4.6 through Bedrock, found both seeded defects, ran activation and completion resolvers, and preserved implementation and specification bytes.
A Claude to Codex to Claude handoff advanced revisions 1, 2, and 3, rejected stale state, demoted inherited verification, and transferred no approval.
